briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Storefronts Rising, Deals Stacking: Michigan Growth Meets National Cannabis Momentum
briefs.top: Michigan operators keep opening doors and eyeing tax relief even as the wholesale-tax fight grinds toward a September trial, while nationally the cannabis and psychedelics sectors are stacking M&A, expansion, and regulatory momentum. A DEA hiccup on rescheduling is real, but it's one speed bump in an otherwise forward-moving week for the industry.

local.text: New Standard throws open its Ann Arbor doors — the operator kicked off a grand-opening weekend with giveaways and discounts to pull in fresh foot traffic.
Bloom City Club expands into Ypsilanti — the Ann Arbor-based operator opened a new Ypsilanti storefront and lined up cannabis-themed events running all October.
Bad Axe could become Michigan's newest market — voters there may soon decide whether to lift a dispensary ban the city has maintained since 2019, opening a fresh retail opportunity.
GOP nominee vows to slash the 24% wholesale tax — John James pledged to repeal or sharply reduce Michigan's cannabis wholesale tax if he wins the governor's race this November.
MiCIA's original tax lawsuit heads to trial this month — the industry group's founding case against the 24% wholesale tax was slated for a September trial, keeping a rollback path alive.

national.text: DEA pumps the brakes on rescheduling review — a DEA administrative law judge paused the marijuana rescheduling hearing after a GAO report flagged process gaps, giving the agency until Oct. 13 to respond.
Curaleaf fires off $270M hostile bid for Aurora — it's the first hostile cross-border cannabis takeover since 2019, though Aurora's board has so far unanimously rejected the offer.

Vireo Growth races toward 270 dispensaries — the multi-state operator is on pace to overtake Trulieve and Curaleaf in store count after a September acquisition spree spanning Florida, Nevada and California.
Trulieve locks up exclusive Connected licensing deal — the multi-state giant announced a master licensing agreement with Connected covering both Florida and Texas.

FDA hearing pushes psilocybin and methylone toward the clinic — regulators solicited public input on supervised therapeutic use, a step toward greenlighting the psychedelic compound and its MDMA-like cousin.
